- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent prices are falling.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) after price spikes; apply downward bias to first 5–7 forecasted days.
- After a sharp price drop, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a slight upward bias in subsequent days if sentiment turns neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model may lag in adjusting; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to forecasted values.
- Model tends to overcorrect after strong sentiment-driven moves; cap forecast adjustments at ±5% of recent 5-day average to avoid overshoot.
